body.statement: Determine whether exact minimum-cost uniform-certificate optimization under the unrestricted charged source interface can use \(2^{O(|\mathcal A|+|\mathrm{LIT}|)}\operatorname{poly}(N_{\mathrm{in}}+N_{\mathcal O})\) time and oracle-answer space, or whether an adversarial pair of finite support oracles forces \(2^{\Omega(B_{\mathrm{cert}})}\) certificate or protocol queries even when \(k\) and \(d\) are fixed.
body.justification: The source interface makes exact optimization well posed but leaves a sharp oracle-complexity frontier between memoized search and information-theoretic lower bounds.
body.gap: Neither fixed-source CTFIDU\({}^{+}\) nor ordinary intervention-design algorithms analyze the query complexity of discovering support-bearing physical protocols through an explicit law oracle.
body.consumer: A positive algorithm would make the certified planner usable on large catalogues, while a lower bound would identify which finite support representation must be added before reviving a treewidth method.
